_meta.purpose: The single shared test corpus for the Urdu bake-off (docs/URDU_BAKEOFF_RESULTS.md). EVERY arm reads its text from this file, so 'same corpus everywhere' is enforced by construction rather than by discipline.
_meta.authoring_rule: `perso_arabic` is the source of truth and was authored first. `roman` and `devanagari` are hand-authored renderings of the SAME sentence — same words, same order, same meaning. Nothing here is a translation: Urdu vocabulary is preserved, so دفتر becomes 'daftar' / दफ़्तर and never an Indian-Hindi synonym like कार्यालय.
_meta.authoring_rule_EXCEPTION_phase_a_items: The 32 items added 2026-08-16 (categories conversational_everyday, ambiguous_spelling, code_switch_heavy, proper_nouns[name_*], numbers_dates[numd_*], messy_realworld, technical_terms[tech_*]) INVERT the rule above, deliberately. They exist to evaluate Roman Urdu -> Perso-Arabic conversion, where the Roman string is the artifact under test — it has to look like what a person actually types, including SMS spellings ('hy', 'nhi', 'q'), dropped vowels, missing punctuation and ALL CAPS. Authoring Perso-Arabic first and rendering it into Roman would have produced tidy, well-formed Roman that no user writes, which is precisely the input the earlier probes were too easy on. So for these items `roman` was authored first as realistic input and `perso_arabic` is the INTENDED READING of it. Consequence: the gold is a judgement call in a way the original 13 are not, and it is the owner's to make — these strings were drafted by Claude and NEED A NATIVE-SPEAKER REVIEW PASS before any number computed against them is quoted as a result.
_meta.devanagari_is_optional_from_2026_08_16: Only the original 13 items carry a `devanagari` field. The 32 Phase-A items omit it and `eval/urdu_represent.py` treats it as optional. Devanagari exists solely to feed IndicF5 arms C/I/J; Hindi is not a target language and hand-authoring 32 more Devanagari renderings would be effort spent on an arm that is still blocked on HuggingFace repo access. Arms that need Devanagari must filter with `CorpusItem.has()` — see urdu_represent.py — and will therefore run on 13 items while Roman/Perso-Arabic arms run on all 45. Do not compare an arm scored over 13 items against one scored over 45.
_meta.why_devanagari_is_hand_authored: Deliberate, and it changes how arms C/I/J must be read. A Perso-Arabic->Devanagari transliterator is genuinely hard (abjad->abugida; Perso-Arabic omits the short vowels Devanagari must write, so it needs vowel restoration). Building a mediocre one first would confound the experiment: a bad result could mean 'the model cannot speak Urdu from Devanagari' OR 'my transliterator is bad', and we could not tell which. Hand-authored gold removes that variable. Arms C/I/J are therefore a CEILING TEST — an upper bound on what any converter could deliver. If a model fails here, the whole Devanagari route is dead and no converter can rescue it. If it succeeds, THEN a real converter is worth building. That ordering is the point.
_meta.two_devanagari_variants: `devanagari` preserves the nuqta forms that carry Urdu phonemes (फ़ ज़ क़ ग़ ख़) and is the arm J 'phonetic / Hindustani' representation. Arm I's plainer transliteration is DERIVED from it at run time by eval/urdu_represent.py's strip_nuqta(), which folds फ़->फ, ज़->ज, क़->क, ग़->ग, ख़->ख — exactly what a naive Hindi-ified transliteration produces. So arms I and J differ in precisely one controlled way: whether Urdu-specific phonemes survive.
_meta.latin_islands: English words (GitHub, pull request, database) are left in Latin script in every representation, matching how a user actually types. Whether a model copes is part of what the code-switching criterion measures — it is not pre-solved here.
_meta.cer_reference_rule: CER for EVERY arm is scored against `perso_arabic`, whatever representation was fed in. The audio is Urdu speech in all arms, so the one canonical Urdu string is the only defensible ground truth; scoring an arm against the Devanagari it happened to be fed would make arm C's CER incomparable to arm B's.
_meta.asr_caveat: Whisper's script choice for Urdu/Hindi audio is unstable and its Urdu is weak. CER here is a SCREEN for gross breakage (silence, wrong language, garbage) — NOT a quality ranking. The decision comes from the blind listening scores; see the plan's 3e/3g.
_meta.reference_axis: Orthogonal to this file. Every item runs against both a male and a female Pakistani Urdu reference clip.
_meta.KNOWN_LIMITATION_ladder_rung_B: Applies to the original 13 items; the Phase-A items have not been re-measured for it. These sentences were authored with correct Urdu codepoints throughout, so eval/urdu_represent.py's normalize_urdu() is a VERIFIED NO-OP on all 13 items (measured: 13/13 unchanged). Ladder rung B — 'Unicode/character normalization only' — therefore cannot be evaluated against this corpus, and a null result for it must NOT be read as 'normalization does not help'. It means the input was already clean. That normalization exists for text a real user types or pastes, which routinely mixes Arabic codepoints (ARABIC YEH U+064A for FARSI YEH U+06CC, ARABIC KAF U+0643 for KEHEH U+06A9, ARABIC HEH U+0647 for HEH GOAL U+06C1) — confirmed working on deliberately dirty input, 4 codepoints folded. To actually test rung B, add dirty variants of these items or source real user-typed Urdu; do not conclude anything about it from this file as it stands.
_meta.arm_I_vs_J_discrimination: Applies to the 13 Devanagari-bearing items only. strip_nuqta() changes 10 of 13 items. The other 3 (owner_03_deadline, owner_04_late, owner_05_github) contain no nuqta consonants, so arms I and J are byte-identical for them and they cannot discriminate between those arms. Expected, not a defect — but exclude them when computing any I-vs-J delta, or the difference will be diluted by three guaranteed ties.
